conflicts.fact: Number of lessons in the unit
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the investigation runs 'over the next 11 lessons', which matches 12 total. Lesson 12 says it is the final lesson of Sub-Strand 3.2, which is consistent, so this is not a real conflict.

Lesson 10 uses approximately Ksh 12.00 per kWh on the domestic lifeline tariff in the bill and learning content, but its Predict card uses Ksh 20 per unit. Lesson 12 uses approximately KES 22 per kWh for the first 50 kWh.

Lesson 10 gives the kettle as 2200 W. Lesson 11 uses a Ramtons kettle drawing 9.2 A at 240 V with a 26 Ω element, which is about 2200 W but not self-consistent (240/26 = 9.23 A, so ~2215 W). Lesson 12 uses a 1,200 W kettle for the Wanjiku house. This is a different household, so it is minor.

conflicts.fact: Cause of the dim lights at restoration
conflicts.versions: Lessons 2 and 8 explain it as internal resistance of the supply, with an Ir drop in the source when current demand is high from many appliances switching on. Lesson 11 explains it as a brownout, where supply voltage was below 240 V, and not as an Ir drop. Lesson 12 says high effective internal resistance in the supply network reduced the terminal voltage.

Lesson 2 uses a 1.5 V AA dry cell. Lesson 8 refers to Lesson 2 measurements but uses a 3 V pack of two D-cells; it also says the Lesson 2 'bulb' was connected, while Lesson 2 used 10 Ω and 47 Ω resistors.

Lesson 9 says students extended their Lesson 6 data tables with a Power column. Lesson 6 data, in a parallel circuit, would show branch resistors, but Lesson 9 claims higher-resistance components dissipated more power for the same current, which is not the parallel-circuit situation (equal voltage); the 'same current' premise matches Lesson 5 series data instead.

Lesson 3 says students return to the model from Lesson 1 (a diagram of the Huruma home circuit), while Lesson 1's model was a particle sketch of the inside of a wire for high versus low current. Lesson 4 describes the Lesson 3 model as a battery, wires and bulb circuit.

conflicts.fact: Voltage across the extension cord branch
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says the cord adds series resistance in one parallel branch, affecting that branch alone, with other branches unaffected. Lesson 7 models the cord in series with the whole parallel strip (bulb and charger share the reduced 208.7 V), so the other branch is affected.
